output.summary: At 13:31 UTC the orders-service was deployed to v2.15.0 (chg:2501) adding a new order‑amendment endpoint. The new validation code assumes every order has a limitPrice; market‑type orders have limitPrice == null, causing a NullPointerException in AmendOrderHandler.validate. The exception appears as 500 errors from orders-service (log pattern F1) and upstream 5xx on edge‑gateway (log pattern F2). Error‑rate spikes from a baseline of ~0.2% to ~6% (metric F3) while all resource metrics stay normal (F4). No config, flag, secret or infra changes occurred in the window (F5). The root cause is a code regression in the newly deployed amendment endpoint.

observations.statement: orders-service logs show a NullPointerException “Cannot invoke BigDecimal.compareTo because order.limitPrice is null” in AmendOrderHandler.validate on PATCH /v1/orders, 447 occurrences, first at 13:33:01 UTC.
edge‑gateway logs record upstream 500 responses from orders-service on route /v1/orders, 420 occurrences, first at 13:34:06 UTC.
orders-service error_rate metric rises from baseline 0.0021 to a mean of 0.019 (peak 0.066) over the incident window.
orders-service CPU, memory, DB‑pool usage and request rate remain within baseline ranges throughout the window.
A single production change occurred: deploy of orders-service v2.15.0 at 13:31:20 UTC (chg:2501) adding the order amendment endpoint.

assumptions.statement: The new amendment endpoint (PATCH /v1/orders) is the only code path that validates order.limitPrice.
assumptions.reason: The stack trace points to AmendOrderHandler.validate; no other handlers reference limitPrice in the diff summary.

assumptions.statement: Market‑type orders legitimately have limitPrice == null and were handled correctly in v2.14.3.
assumptions.reason: The incident only affects price/quantity edits (amend), not order creation, implying the previous version accepted null limitPrice.

assumptions.statement: The deploy at 13:31 UTC was fully rolled out before the first NPE at 13:33 UTC (typical rollout < 2 min).
assumptions.reason: Observed onset aligns with deploy timestamp; no delayed rollout indicated.

assumptions.statement: No hidden configuration change, feature‑flag flip, or secret rotation accompanied the deploy.
assumptions.reason: Change history for orders-service and edge‑gateway shows only the deploy (chg:2501) in the 45‑minute window.

hypotheses.mechanism: The v2.15.0 amendment endpoint validates order.limitPrice without a null check. Market orders have null limitPrice, causing a NullPointerException that bubbles up as HTTP 500. Edge‑gateway propagates these as upstream 5xx, producing the observed customer‑facing errors.
predictions: Rolling back to v2.14.3 will immediately drop error_rate to baseline.
Adding a null guard for limitPrice in AmendOrderHandler will eliminate the NPE on re‑deploy.

hypotheses.mechanism: A configuration change or feature‑flag enabled stricter validation that rejects null limitPrice.
predictions: A config/flag change would appear in change history; none does.

hypotheses.mechanism: Degraded market‑data service returns malformed order objects lacking limitPrice, leading to NPE.
predictions: Market‑data error_rate or latency would spike; metrics show none.

hypotheses.mechanism: Thread‑pool or DB‑pool exhaustion corrupts request state, causing null limitPrice.
predictions: CPU, memory, or DB‑pool metrics would show saturation; they do not.
